closureBasis: Gate 10 can be recorded GREEN on this receipt, bound for the first time to the rc18 candidate, and gate 5 -- the one substantive question -- is GREEN on the shipped bytes and independently reproduced. omega#26 still cannot close: gate 2 is NOT established on this candidate. Its only evidence is host-level and bound to the rc15 host binary, the host binary changed, and the change touches the Full Auto host surfaces gate 2 exercises; the producer's own carry rule forbids inheriting it. Separately, gate 2's own record says no person watched the run, so the 'owner-real' half is unmet regardless of candidate. Closure is the coordinator's act, and this reviewer does not close the obligation it has just admitted.

Everything upstream of the paint is proven -- the engine emits the note addressed to the target thread, the host no longer refuses it, the renderer and its element id are compiled into the shipped binary, and the renderer is guarded against being hidden behind an expander, tooltip or hover.

The reviewer checked whether a SAFE headless route existed and found none: crates/zed/src/visual_test_runner.rs at rc18 registers nine visual scenes (front door, executor disclosure, route pin) and none covers a system note. git grep for system_note/SystemNote in visual_test_runner.rs returns nothing. The finding itself is exemplary: it names the binding at assets/keymaps/default-macos.json:711, states that synthesized keystrokes do not reach the action, and supplies the two controls that make the negative meaningful (other chords work in the same session; no enabled macOS symbolic hotkey claims keycode 50). However it does NOT appear in the record's own 'What still blocks a close' list, which names only three gaps, and the Scope table marks the terminal row 'covered' with no caveat.
